report:
Pituitary tumour, transsphenoidal excision

Received in formalin are fragments of soft tumour tissue, measuring 18 x 12 x 4 mm in aggregate. The specimen is entirely embedded; see block key.

(1-2) Tumour fragments.

Specimen and tumour
- Procedure: Transsphenoidal pituitary tumour resection
- Tumour integrity: Fragmented
- Tumour number: Single pituitary neuroendocrine tumour
- Tumour size: 32 mm in greatest dimension (imaging)

Microscopic findings
- Tumour type and subtype: PIT1-lineage pituitary neuroendocrine tumour,
  somatotroph tumour, sparsely granulated
- Tumour histology:
  Sections show a pituitary neuroendocrine tumour composed of monotonous cells arranged in diffuse sheets and perivascular pseudorosettes, with chromophobic cytoplasm and round to oval nuclei with finely granular chromatin. Fibrous bodies are present. Reticulin shows loss of the normal acinar architecture. On immunohistochemistry, the tumour cells are diffusely positive for synaptophysin, PIT1 and GH, focally positive for PRL, and negative for TPIT and SF1. Low-molecular-weight keratin (CAM5.2) is diffusely positive, with fibrous bodies in more than 70% of tumour cells.
- Ki-67 labelling index: 4%
- Mitotic count: 1 per 2 mm2
- Histologically confirmed invasion: Present (bone and sinonasal mucosa)
- Non-tumorous pituitary: Not identified

Additional findings
- None identified

  PIT1-lineage
